intro: A folk-noir songwriter.
story: A.A. Bondy was a respected folk-noir songwriter, with Believers on Fat Possum in 2011 behind him, when he played Pickathon in 2012. He stepped away from music for several years and returned with Enderness in 2019, and still surfaces for select festivals such as Hardly Strictly Bluegrass.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 5:15 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 4, 7 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: An old-time banjoist already admired.
story: Abigail Washburn was already admired in old-time circles, with City of Refuge on Rounder in 2011, when she played Pickathon in 2012. With Bela Fleck she made a duo record that won the Grammy for Best Folk Album in 2016, and she has kept her long conversation with the guzheng player Wu Fei going.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 5:30 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 4, 3:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A psych-folk songwriter, here for the fourth time.
story: Alela Diane played Pickathon in 2007, 2009 and 2011 before she came back in 2012, after To Be Still on Rough Trade. Cusp followed in 2018, and she returned in 2018 and 2026. Settled in Portland, she released Who's Keeping Time? on Loose in 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 5 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 5, 3 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Portland band, back after Furr.
story: Blitzen Trapper had played Pickathon in 2009, fresh from the success of Furr on Sub Pop, and returned in 2012. Eric Earley has kept the band moving, mining old 1990s four-track tapes for 100's of 1000's, Millions of Billions, and touring through 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 9 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 6:45 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A young Tuareg guitar talent from Niger.
story: Omara Bombino Moctar was introduced to Pickathon audiences in 2012 as a rising Tuareg guitar talent from Niger. Nomad followed on Nonesuch in 2013, Azel in 2016 and Sahel in 2023, both on Partisan, and a Grammy nomination came for Deran in 2019. He still carries the music of Niger to stages across Europe and North America.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 8 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 5, 11:30 am, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 6 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A North Carolina indie-folk band.
story: Bowerbirds are a North Carolina indie-folk band who played Pickathon in 2012, around their third album, The Clearing. After a long hiatus and lineup changes, founder Phil Moore returned with becalmyounglovers in 2021.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 7:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 4, 12:45 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: An Appalachian fiddle master, back after 2011.
story: Bruce Molsky is a master of Appalachian fiddle, banjo and song who had been playing since 1989, and he played Pickathon in 2011 and 2012. He shared a Grammy nomination for Fiddlers 4 with Michael Doucet, Darol Anger and Rushad Eggleston, and he keeps teaching and touring with string-band luminaries.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 6:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 5, 4:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 7 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Twin-fiddle Cajun dancehall veterans.
story: Cajun Country Revival were formed by veterans of the Louisiana roots scene and brought twin-fiddle dancehall energy to Pickathon in 2012. They still bring traditional Prairie Cajun music to attentive listening venues and regional stages.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 8:30 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 4, 6 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A Northwest swing and jazz staple.
story: Casey MacGill is a staple of Northwest swing and jazz who brought his ukulele and cornet charm to Pickathon in 2003, 2010 and 2012. He is a fixture in Seattle, still playing neighborhood venues.
sets: Sun Aug 5, 11 am, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 5, 6:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: An elusive indie-rock traveler.
story: Cass McCombs was an elusive indie-rock traveler, with Wit's End and Humor Risk both on Domino in 2011, when he played Pickathon in 2012. Mangy Love followed on Anti- in 2016, and he came back to the farm that year. Heartmind came in 2022 and the double album Interior Live Oak in 2025, with a tour of Europe and North America in 2026.
sets: Sun Aug 5, late night (12:30 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 5, 2:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A towering voice in traditional bluegrass.
story: Danny Paisley was already a towering voice of traditional bluegrass when he played Pickathon in 2012. He and the Southern Grass have never strayed from hard-driving, unadorned mountain music, and they keep recording and touring regularly.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 4:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 4, 11 am, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Toronto songwriter and quiet craftsman.
story: Doug Paisley is a Toronto folk songwriter and quiet craftsman whose Constant Companion was on the 2011 Polaris Prize long list, and he played Pickathon in 2012. He has kept an unhurried pace, with Strong Feelings in 2014 and Starter Home in 2018, and released Sad Old World in 2024.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 4 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 4, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: Harmony-drenched psych-pop from Philadelphia, here for a third time.
story: Dr. Dog had played Pickathon in 2009 and 2010 before they returned in 2012, the year of Be the Void on Anti-, after Shame, Shame in 2010. They stepped back from full-time touring in 2021 and surprised fans with a self-titled comeback in 2024, with selected festival and theater dates into 2027.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 9:45 pm, Mountain View Stage · Mon Aug 6, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: A Portland old-time band, here for the sixth time.
story: Foghorn Stringband played Pickathon in 2002, 2003, 2005, 2009, 2010 and again in 2012, then in 2013 and 2016, an old-time collective in Portland who became a cornerstone of the stringband revival. They still tour internationally.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: Quebecois fiddle, flute and foot percussion.
story: Genticorum are a trio of Quebecois fiddle, flute and foot percussion who brought their kinetic folk traditions to Pickathon in 2012. More than twenty years into their run they remain a mainstay of the international Celtic and folk circuits.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 5 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 5, 12 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 4:15 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: Erika Wennerstrom's powerhouse band, back after 2010.
story: Heartless Bastards are Erika Wennerstrom's band, who rose from Cincinnati clubs to Pickathon in 2010, returned in 2012 and again in 2015. The Mountain came in 2009 on Fat Possum and A Beautiful Life in 2021. Wennerstrom, now in Austin, toured for the twentieth anniversary of All This Time.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 8:45 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 5, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: A New Orleans brass institution.
story: Hot 8 Brass Band were already a New Orleans brass institution when they played Pickathon in 2012. A Grammy nomination for Best Regional Roots Music Album came in 2014. They have weathered profound loss and keep the second-line tradition alive, touring worldwide and honoring their late bandleader Bennie Pete in new recordings.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 3 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 4, 6 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 5, 11:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: London siblings of vintage analog R&B.
story: Kitty, Daisy & Lewis are London siblings with a vintage analog approach to R&B, blues and rockabilly, and a multi-instrumental show that came to Pickathon in 2012. They continue to tour internationally, across Europe and Australia.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 7 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 5, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A scrappy conservatory quartet.
story: Lake Street Dive were a scrappy, conservatory-bred quartet winning crowds one set at a time when they played Pickathon in 2012, and they came back in 2013. The Americana Music Association nominated them for Duo/Group of the Year in 2014 and 2016. Side Pony followed in 2016 and Good Together in 2024, and What About Flamingos? is due in February 2027.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 11 pm, Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 5, 12:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 5, 6 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A heart-on-sleeve songwriter, here for the fourth time.
story: Langhorne Slim played Pickathon in 2007, 2008 and 2010 before he returned in 2012, with a self-titled album on Kemado in 2008 behind him, and he played again in 2015. He is a tireless live performer who has toured theaters and festivals, with a 2027 tour supporting Grace Potter.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 5:15 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 4, 8:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A quiet standout of Portland folk.
story: Laura Gibson was a quiet standout of Portland's folk scene when she played Pickathon in 2008, and she returned in 2009 and 2012. She went on to earn an MFA in fiction while releasing records that drew praise, and in late 2026 she signed with Loose Music and released the single Sylvia.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 3:30 pm, Mountain View Stage · Fri Aug 3, 6:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sat Aug 4, 2 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A Raleigh Southern indie band.
story: Lonnie Walker are Raleigh roots-rockers with a gritty Southern indie sound, who played Pickathon in 2012. Their output has been sporadic since Earth Canals in 2015, but the band still reunites for select live shows.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 7 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 1:30 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Torchbearers of Veracruz's son jarocho.
story: Los Cojolites carry the son jarocho tradition of Veracruz and brought a participatory fandango spirit to Pickathon in 2012. Grammy nominations came for Sembrando Flores and for Zapateando. They continue to share traditional Mexican music and community dance gatherings across North America.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage · Sat Aug 4, 12 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 8 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

act: Lost Bayou Ramblers ft Gordon Gano
intro: A Cajun band pushing into punk territory.
story: Lost Bayou Ramblers played Pickathon in 2009 and again in 2012, joined by Gordon Gano of the Violent Femmes, already pushing Cajun music toward punk. They returned in 2018. Their album Kalenda won the Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album, and they remain champions of Louisiana French culture.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 11:45 am, Mountain View Stage

intro: A quirky North Carolina duo.
story: Midtown Dickens are a North Carolina duo whose quirky, homemade folk-pop played Pickathon in 2012. After years of quiet they resurfaced in June 2025 with a new collection, Lanterns.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 11 am, Workshop Barn · Mon Aug 6, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage

intro: An indie and alt-country icon.
story: Neko Case was already an indie and alt-country icon, with Fox Confessor Brings the Flood in 2006 and Middle Cyclone in 2009, which drew a Grammy nomination for Best Contemporary Folk Album, when she played Pickathon in 2012. The Worse Things Get came in 2013 and Hell-On in 2018. She self-produced Neon Grey Midnight Green in 2025.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 9 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 8:45 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: Vancouver hillbilly swing and yodeling.
story: Petunia and the Vipers are a Vancouver band of hillbilly swing, ragtime and yodeling who brought eccentric retro charm to Pickathon in 2012. They are still logging highway miles up and down the West Coast.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 12:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 5, 1 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Matthew Houck's indie-folk, just before Muchacho.
story: Matthew Houck brought Phosphorescent to Pickathon in 2012, just before Muchacho on Dead Oceans in 2013, and returned in 2018, the year of C'est La Vie. Revelator came on Verve in 2024. Now in Nashville, he keeps writing, scoring films and touring.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 4:15 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 5, 5:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Texas country bluesman of gospel-tinged boogie.
story: Reverend KM Williams is a Texas country bluesman who brought gospel-inflected boogie to Pickathon in 2012. There are no recent albums or public tour dates.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 2:45 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 4, 1 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A young Houston traditionalist.
story: Robert Ellis was a young Houston traditionalist, with Photographs on New West in 2011 and an Americana Music Association emerging-act nomination in 2012, when he played Pickathon that year. The Lights from the Chemical Plant, in 2014, was nominated for Album of the Year. Texas Piano Man followed in 2019, and he still tours solo, road-testing songs about fatherhood.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 2:30 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 11:30 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A Charleston duo at the edge of their breakout.
story: Shovels & Rope are Michael Trent and Cary Ann Hearst of Charleston, who arrived at Pickathon in 2012 on the cusp of O' Be Joyful, and the Americana Music Association named them Emerging Act of the Year in 2013, with a nomination for Album of the Year. Swimmin' Time followed in 2014 and Little Seeds in 2016. They came back in 2018 and host festivals of their own.
sets: Sun Aug 5, 2:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 5, 5 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: Palm-wine reggae from refugee camps.
story: Sierra Leone's Refugee All Stars formed in West African refugee camps and brought uplifting palm-wine reggae to Pickathon in 2012. Their last studio album was Libation in 2014, and the group has largely been off the road.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 1:45 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: Sonny Smith's San Francisco garage-pop.
story: Sonny & the Sunsets is Sonny Smith's wry, sun-bleached San Francisco garage-pop band, who played Pickathon in 2011, returned in 2012 and again in 2015. Smith works across music, plays and visual art, and has kept the band going for over fifteen years.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 4, 6 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 3:15 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: An Ohio indie-folk band with an Appalachian concept album.
story: Southeast Engine are an Ohio indie-folk band who played Pickathon in 2012 behind Canary, an Appalachian concept album. The group has been dormant for over a decade, and in 2024 the frontman Adam Remnant released solo work with his band the Signs.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 1 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 4, 11:30 am, Galaxy Barn

intro: Traditional family-style bluegrass.
story: Ted Jones is a North Carolina native who led The Tarheel Boys through traditional family-style bluegrass and gospel for fifteen years. They played Pickathon in 2012, and he retired the band in August 2019. No recent news has surfaced.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 1:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 11 am, Workshop Barn

intro: A harp-laced Montreal band.
story: The Barr Brothers are a harp-laced Montreal band who stood out at Pickathon in 2012, the year their self-titled album made the Polaris Prize long list, and returned in 2014. They have built an international following and returned with their fourth studio album, Let It Hiss.
sets: Sat Aug 4, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 5, 7:30 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Brothers with Everly-style blood harmonies.
story: The Cactus Blossoms are the brothers Jack Torrey and Page Burkum, whose Everly-style blood harmonies were a Midwestern secret when they played Pickathon in 2012. They came back in 2013 and 2025. You're Dreaming came on Red House in 2016, and after a Twin Peaks cameo they released Every Time I Think About You in 2024.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 2:30 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A Seattle trio of gritty, rhythmic folk-rock.
story: The Cave Singers formed from several Northwest indie bands and played Pickathon in 2008, 2010 and 2012, after Welcome Joy on Matador in 2009. They no longer tour as relentlessly, though the Seattle trio still reconvenes for hometown shows.
sets: Sat Aug 4, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 4, 4:30 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Laura Burhenn's politically charged indie pop.
story: The Mynabirds is Laura Burhenn, whose soulful, politically charged indie pop came to Pickathon in 2012 around Generals on Saddle Creek. Be Here Now followed in 2017, and she still shares periodic singles under the name.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 12 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 5, 10 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A swing duo of upright bass and tenor guitar.
story: Andy Bean and Fuller Condon are The Two Man Gentlemen Band, a witty swing duo of upright bass and tenor guitar, who played Pickathon in 2007 and again in 2012. They composed the theme for Disney's Wander Over Yonder, and released their last album in 2014.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 1:45 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 5, 2 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: An ascending indie-rock band.
story: The War on Drugs were an ascending indie-rock band, a year after Slave Ambient on Secretly Canadian, when they played Pickathon in 2012, and they returned in 2014, the year of Lost in the Dream. A Deeper Understanding, in 2017, won the Grammy for Best Rock Album. Adam Granduciel's widescreen rock now fills major stages.
sets: Sun Aug 5, 1:30 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 5, 8:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A brotherly duo, newly under way, here for a third time.
story: Chris and Oliver Wood were just launching their acoustic duo when they played Pickathon in 2006, and they returned in 2007 and 2012. Now a roots trio with the drummer Jano Rix, they earned a Grammy nomination for Best Americana Album in 2019 and released their ninth album, Puff of Smoke, in 2025.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 7:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 5, 5 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: John Dwyer's relentless psych-punk band.
story: Thee Oh Sees were already underground heroes for their relentless live shows when they played Pickathon in 2012, and they returned in 2016. John Dwyer's band has cycled through spellings and is now billed as Osees, one of psych-punk's hardest-working live acts.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 4, 2:30 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: Seattle's cosmic Afrofuturist hip-hop and soul duo.
story: THEESatisfaction were a Seattle hip-hop and soul duo whose cosmic Afrofuturism came to Pickathon in 2012. Stasia Irons and Catherine Harris-White split amicably in 2017 and have pursued solo careers as Stas THEE Boss and SassyBlack.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 9 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sun Aug 5, 4 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Portland-born folk storyteller.
story: Todd Snider was a beloved folk storyteller long before he played Pickathon in 2012, the year of Agnostic Hymns & Stoner Fables, blending sharp humor with empathy since East Nashville Skyline. The Americana Music Association had nominated him for Artist of the Year in 2007. He died in November 2025, and a posthumous album, My Second Rodeo, followed.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 2 pm, Workshop Barn · Fri Aug 3, 4:30 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A Portland orchestral indie-rock collective.
story: Typhoon are a Portland orchestral indie-rock collective led by Kyle Morton, who broke out nationally around their 2010 Pickathon appearance, and played again in 2012. White Lighter came in 2013 on Roll Call and Offerings in 2018. In September 2026 they returned home for a pastoral outdoor set on Sauvie Island.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 8 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 4, 3 pm, Woods Stage

intro: Hyper-agile psychedelic garage rock from Austin.
story: White Denim are an Austin band of hyper-agile psychedelic garage rock who played Pickathon in 2012, after D on Downtown in 2011. Corsicana Lemonade followed in 2013, Stiff in 2016 and Performance in 2018, through countless lineups around James Petralli. They followed 12, in 2024, with another studio record in 2026.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 6:15 pm, Fir Meadows Stage · Sat Aug 4, 11:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Michigan honky-tonker with Waylon in his bones.
story: Whitey Morgan is a Michigan honky-tonker whose Waylon-indebted country came to Pickathon in 2011, and he returned in 2012 and 2015. True to his blue-collar approach, he has stayed on the highway, booking club dates across North America through late 2026 and into 2027.
sets: Fri Aug 3, 7 pm, Mountain View Stage · Fri Aug 3, 11:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Portland band led by Luz Elena Mendoza.
story: Y La Bamba is Luz Elena Mendoza's Portland band of experimental folk-pop, a hometown favorite when it played Pickathon in 2012, and it returned in 2017. Mujeres came in 2019, and Lucha on Tender Loving Empire in 2023.
sets: Sat Aug 4, 4 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 5, 12:45 pm, Fir Meadows Stage

intro: A Portland country-rock band with three songwriters.
story: denver is a Portland country-rock band with a working-class, three-songwriter attack, who played Pickathon in 2012. The band has been inactive for years.
